prompt: Earth's escape velocity is about 11.2 kilometres per second. What does that number actually mean for a projectile launched from Earth's surface, ignoring air resistance?

options.text: It is the speed a projectile needs so that Earth's gravity will never pull it back, even without any further push
It is the fastest speed any object is allowed to travel in space
It is the speed of a satellite in the lowest possible orbit
It depends strongly on the projectile's mass, so heavier craft need a much higher speed

explanation: At escape velocity a projectile's kinetic energy is enough for it to climb out of Earth's gravitational well indefinitely without extra thrust. Ignoring air resistance, the value does not depend on the projectile's own mass.
